# Switch

Figma: [03g. Switch](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-902) · Family: 03 Form & Input · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-24

A binary on/off toggle for instant-apply settings. The user taps to flip a single state - no confirmation, no submit button. Used for preferences that should take effect immediately: notifications on/off, dark mode, biometric login, two-factor authentication. Compare with Checkbox (deferred apply via submit button) - Switch commits the change on tap.

### Switch Indicator

The pill track and sliding thumb atom of a switch (thumb right means on in both directions).

Level: atom · Part of: Switch

Use when:
- Inside Switch
- Toggle slot of ListItem or ActionList rows where the row text is the label

Don't use when:
- A labelled toggle: use Switch

Accessibility: Expose as a switch with on/off state and a name from the row label.

### Switch

A labelled on/off toggle that applies the setting immediately with no submit button.

Level: organism · Contains: Switch Indicator

Use when:
- Notification channel preferences
- Face ID or biometric login, 2FA on/off
- Auto-invest or marketing opt-in settings
- Settings forced by policy: State=disabled-on with a helper

Don't use when:
- The value is saved on submit (terms acceptance, form answers): use Checkbox
- Picking one of several options: use Radio Group or SegmentedControl_2/_3
- Several independent options in a form: use Checkbox Group

Accessibility: Do not flip the thumb in RTL, and confirm risky changes (turning off 2FA) because the toggle commits instantly.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Switch is the standard control for binary on/off settings where the change takes effect immediately. Visually a pill-shaped track with a sliding circular thumb - left position means off, right means on. Always paired with a label that describes what the toggle controls.

On Safqah, Switch shows up on: notification preferences ("Email me about new deals" - instant on/off), biometric login toggle, dark mode toggle, two-factor authentication on/off, marketing communications opt-in, auto-investment toggle. The unifying pattern: tap → setting applies → no further confirmation needed.

### At a glance

### Atomic architecture

Switch follows the same atomic pattern as Checkbox and Radio. One atom (Indicator) and one organism (Switch).

Atom - Switch Indicator · 24 variants

The track + sliding thumb. Variants: 3 sizes × 8 states (off / on / hover-off / hover-on / focus-off / focus-on / disabled-off / disabled-on). Direction-agnostic - on/off positions are universal, not tied to text direction. Reused inside the Switch organism as an exposed instance.

Organism - Switch · 48 variants

Composes Indicator + Label (text) + optional Helper text below. Variants: 3 sizes × 8 states × 2 directions. The Direction axis flips the indicator and label order - LTR shows [switch label]; RTL shows [label switch]. Indicator is exposed so state can be controlled through the organism props.

### Sizes

Three sizes match Checkbox/Radio conventions for visual rhythm across the form family. lg for primary touch contexts, md for standard density, sm for compact tables/dense settings.

Large (52×28 track, 20 thumb, font 16dp)

Primary settings on mobile - notification toggles, dark mode, biometric login. Pairs with lg Input/Checkbox/Radio. Track easily meets WCAG 2.5.5 AAA touch target.

Medium (44×24 track, 16 thumb, font 14dp)

Standard desktop density - settings page rows, profile preference panels. Most common choice for dense desktop UIs.

Small (36×20 track, 14 thumb, font 14dp)

Compact contexts - table column toggles, dense filter panels. Use sparingly on mobile - track height of 20dp is below WCAG 2.5.5 AA minimum; rely on row tap area to compensate.

### States

Eight states cover the full lifecycle for both on and off positions. Hover and focus get separate variants for each position so the visual cue is unambiguous about which side of the toggle the user is interacting with.

off

Default off position. Track fills with bg/disabled (gray), thumb on the leading edge. Tap to switch on.

on

Active. Track fills with bg/brand/primary (green), thumb slides to the trailing edge. The primary "yes" affordance.

hover-off

Cursor/touch hover while off. Track darkens to border/strong - subtle cue that the toggle is interactive.

hover-on

Cursor/touch hover while on. Track stays green (same as on) - the "on" state already communicates interactivity.

focus-off

Keyboard focus while off. 2dp dark focus ring outside the track.

focus-on

Keyboard focus while on. 2dp focus ring outside the green track.

disabled-off

Inert off state. Track at bg/disabled with 50% opacity. Label uses text/muted.

disabled-on

Inert on state. Green track at 50% opacity. Use when the value is locked on by another control or tier constraint.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Switch flips its internal layout for Arabic. The track and thumb stay visually consistent (on means right-thumb in BOTH directions - the on/off semantic is universal). What flips is the position of the entire indicator relative to the label.

LTR

Default. Indicator on the leading (left) edge, label after. Thumb slides right for on. Standard for English contexts.

RTL

Arabic context. Label first, indicator on the trailing (visually right) edge. Thumb still slides right for on - on/off positions are universal, not direction-dependent.

> **Tip:** Important: the thumb position (left for off, right for on) does NOT flip in RTL. This is a Material 3 / iOS convention - the on/off visual is meant to be universal, not language-dependent. Flipping the thumb position in RTL would confuse users coming from native iOS/Android Arabic apps.

### Code examples

How to consume Switch in Flutter.

### Flutter - basic Switch

```dart
// Standard notification preference toggle
SafqahSwitch(
  value: _emailNotifications,
  label: 'Email me about new deals',
  onChanged: (value) {
    setState(() => _emailNotifications = value);
    // Instant apply - persist immediately
    _settings.updateNotificationPreference(
      type: NotificationType.email,
      enabled: value,
    );
  },
)
```

### Flutter - switch with helper text

```dart
// Switch with explanatory helper
SafqahSwitch(
  value: _biometricEnabled,
  label: 'Biometric login',
  showHelper: true,
  helperText: 'Use Face ID or fingerprint to unlock the app',
  onChanged: (value) async {
    if (value) {
      // Need to prompt for permission first
      final granted = await BiometricService.requestPermission();
      if (granted) {
        setState(() => _biometricEnabled = true);
      }
    } else {
      setState(() => _biometricEnabled = false);
    }
  },
)
```

### Flutter - locked switch (forced on)

```dart
// Disabled-on for enterprise-locked features
SafqahSwitch(
  value: true,
  label: 'Two-factor authentication',
  showHelper: true,
  helperText: user.isEnterprise
    ? 'Required by your organization'
    : null,
  enabled: !user.isEnterprise,  // disabled = forced on for enterprise
  onChanged: user.isEnterprise ? null : (value) {
    setState(() => _twoFactorEnabled = value);
  },
)
```

### Flutter - RTL Arabic context

```dart
// Arabic locale - switch flips to indicator-on-right
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: SafqahSwitch(
    value: _darkMode,
    label: 'الوضع الداكن',  // "Dark mode"
    onChanged: (value) => setState(() {
      _darkMode = value;
      ThemeService.setMode(value ? ThemeMode.dark : ThemeMode.light);
    }),
  ),
)
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts.

- **Do** · Instant-apply settings: Use Switch when the change should take effect immediately on tap - notification preferences, dark mode, biometric login. No submit button needed; the toggle IS the commit.
- **Don't** · Instant-apply settings: Don't use Switch for form fields that need a submit step. Use Checkbox - Checkbox semantics ("I will commit this on submit") match deferred-apply patterns. Switch would mislead users into thinking the value already applied.
- **Do** · Binary on/off only: Use Switch for single yes/no values: this feature is enabled, this preference is on. The pill shape signals "two states, pick one".
- **Don't** · Binary on/off only: Don't use Switch for multi-option selection - use Radio. Don't use Switch for multiple independent toggles in a group - use Checkbox so the group reads as multi-select.
- **Do** · Arabic RTL settings: RTL direction. Label first (reads right-to-left), indicator on the trailing edge. Thumb still slides right for on - matches native iOS/Android Arabic conventions where on/off positions are universal.
- **Don't** · Arabic RTL settings: Don't use LTR direction in Arabic contexts. Don't flip the thumb position in RTL either - that breaks user expectations from native Arabic apps where the on-position is always on the right.
- **Do** · Forced enterprise setting: Disabled-on when a setting is forced by tier/policy (e.g. enterprise requires 2FA always on). Show the value as on, label/track at 50% opacity, with helper text explaining "Required by your organization".
- **Don't** · Forced enterprise setting: Don't leave a forced setting in active state - user taps to turn off, nothing happens, looks broken. Don't hide the setting entirely - user can't see what's active.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Info:** Switch / Checkbox / Radio share the same atomic pattern (Indicator atom + organism with Label + Helper). All three controls feel like a coherent family in forms. Switch differs in: pill-shaped track instead of square box/circle, on/off semantics instead of multi-select/single-select, instant apply instead of deferred submit.

> **Info:** Direction handling: the Switch organism flips indicator/label order in RTL, but the indicator itself (thumb position) does NOT flip. On = thumb right, off = thumb left, regardless of LTR/RTL. This matches Material 3 and iOS conventions where on/off is a universal visual, not a language-dependent one. Tested against native iOS Settings in Arabic - same convention.

> **Info:** Off-state track uses bg/disabled (gray) intentionally. Some design systems use a darker neutral or even a tinted gray for off-state - Safqah uses bg/disabled because it reads consistently with Checkbox/Radio disabled states, creating visual coherence across the form family. Trade-off: off-state and disabled-off can look similar at a glance; the difference is opacity (100% vs 50%).

> **Info:** Indicator is exposed as a nested instance on every Switch organism variant. Atom-level state (the State prop on Indicator) can be controlled through the organism props OR through the variant axis. Both are wired in - useful when you need to flip state programmatically through props.

> **Info:** Helper text Show Helper boolean ships as false by default. Most switches are simple label + toggle. Helper is for cases where the on/off action needs additional context (e.g. "Selecting biometric login will trigger permission prompt on first use" - explanatory rather than warning).

> **Warning:** Track dimensions are raw px (52×28, 44×24, 36×20). These are NOT bound to size primitives - there's no dedicated "switch-track-width" / "switch-track-height" variable in DS. If you change Switch sizing globally, update the helper SIZES dict in the build script and rebuild. Flagged for cleanup when component-specific size tokens get added.

> **Info:** Thumb position is hardcoded based on State variant - left for off, right for on. Not data-driven via a prop. Means: if you want to override thumb position dynamically, you swap the entire variant. For pure visual demos this is fine; for runtime control the framework (Flutter SafqahSwitch widget) handles the animation between positions.

> **Warning:** sm size (20dp track height) fails WCAG 2.5.5 AA for the track alone - but the label tap area extends the effective target. Same flag as Checkbox/Radio sm sizes. Use only in dense desktop UIs where row tap area is the actual target.

> **Warning:** FONT WORKAROUND - Same as the rest of the form family. Label uses IBM Plex Sans Regular since Font/Family/Base resolves to IBM Plex Sans Arabic (not installed). Font/Size, Font/Line-Height, and Font/Weight all bound to variables on every text node.
